sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which important place in our neighbourhood helps us buy our daily groceries and vegetables?
Which of these nutrients gives our body quick energy to play and study all day?
People who live near our houses in the same community are called our:
Which of the following is a non-living thing you might find while on a nature trail?
What do plants need directly from the environment to make their own food?
Which of these foods is highly rich in protein and helps our body repair and grow?
Where do we immediately go if someone in our neighbourhood is very sick or injured?
What is the green substance in plant leaves that helps them prepare food?
A small family that consists of only parents and their children living together is called a:
Drinking plenty of water daily is essential for our health mostly because it helps to:
Why is it important to share household chores with your family members while living together? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Sharing chores reduces the burden on one person, keeps the house clean, and teaches teamwork and responsibility to everyone in the family.

questions.question_text: Mention two important services provided by a fire station to the neighbourhood during an emergency. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A fire station quickly sends fire engines to put out dangerous fires and helps rescue people or animals trapped inside burning buildings.

questions.question_text: Name two items you should carry when going on a nature trail and explain why. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: You should carry a water bottle to stay fully hydrated and a magnifying glass to observe small insects and leaf textures closely.

questions.question_text: How do large trees help in keeping the environment clean for us to breathe? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Trees absorb harmful carbon dioxide gas from the dirty air and release fresh oxygen, which humans and animals need to breathe and stay alive.

questions.question_text: Why should we avoid eating too much junk food like chips and cold drinks regularly? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Junk food contains excessive oil, sugar, and salt but lacks essential vitamins. Eating it regularly can make our bodies unhealthy, lazy, and weak.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are planning a healthy lunchbox for your school picnic. Describe the food items you will pack to ensure a balanced diet. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would pack a vegetable sandwich made with brown bread for energy. I would include a fresh apple for essential vitamins and a small portion of almonds for healthy fats. Finally, I would carry fresh homemade lemonade to stay properly hydrated during the picnic.

questions.question_text: Imagine a new family has moved into your neighbourhood. Describe three ways you and your parents can make them feel welcome and comfortable. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: We can go to their house to introduce ourselves with a warm smile. We can offer them a delicious home-cooked meal on their first day and invite their children to play in the community park so they make new friends quickly.

questions.question_text: Describe a step-by-step plan to organize a cleanliness drive in your neighbourhood park, including how to involve your neighbours. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, I will create colorful posters about the cleanliness drive and put them on the society notice board. Then, I will request my neighbours to gather on Sunday morning with gloves and garbage bags. We will divide into groups, pick up dry waste, and pledge to keep the park spotless.

questions.question_text: Explain how quietly observing insects and birds during a nature trail helps us understand the food chain in our local environment. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: By quietly watching nature, we can see real-life food chains in action. For example, we might observe a green caterpillar eating a fresh leaf. Later, we might see a small bird swooping down to eat that same caterpillar. This shows how all living things depend on each other for survival.
